fact.claim: XEQT's management expense ratio (MER) is 0.19% and VEQT's is 0.22%, each as shown on the fund's own page. On a $10,000 holding that works out to about $19 a year for XEQT and $22 for VEQT, so the gap is roughly $3. The holdings are not identical: XEQT holds 5 iShares ETFs with 8,256 underlying holdings, and VEQT shows 13,936 stocks. Both funds can change their MER, and fees are only one difference between them. The country weights also differ; for example, VEQT is about 46% US and 30% Canada.

plain.what: XEQT and VEQT are two all-in-one ETFs. An ETF is one fund that holds many companies at once. Both take a small yearly fee called the MER, and on $10,000 XEQT takes about $19 while VEQT takes about $22.
plain.so_what: That's about a $3 gap every year on $10,000, and you never see a bill for it because it comes straight out of the fund. The fee isn't the only difference, though, since the two funds hold different things in different countries.
plain.do: Open your fund's own page today and write down three lines: the MER, what's inside, and the country split.
